memories.title: A public memory boundary takes shape
memories.excerpt: The memory system now separates private candidates from a deliberately small public projection.
memories.significance: The website can preserve meaningful progress without becoming a window into private working context.

memories.title: Evidence before claims becomes a publication rule
memories.excerpt: A working principle from the Field Log is now enforced at the public-memory boundary.
memories.significance: Every published memory must retain a public, inspectable trail without exposing its private source material.

memories.title: The website learns to show relationships
memories.excerpt: Projects, writing, and field notes can now be explored as connected evidence rather than isolated pages.
memories.significance: The archive begins to reflect how the work actually develops: through linked questions, artifacts, and decisions.

memories.title: The desk becomes a public workbench
memories.excerpt: The site shifts from a portfolio display toward an editorial surface for active investigation.
memories.significance: Finished work and work in progress can share one durable archive while remaining clearly labeled.

memories.title: Bridget's role is narrowed to reconciliation
memories.excerpt: Bridget coordinates significance, review, and publication while source systems remain responsible for their facts.
memories.significance: Clear ownership keeps the memory pipeline portable and prevents one coordinator from becoming an untraceable source of truth.
